The test image shows a corn ear with:
- White fungal mycelium visible near the base of the ear
- Brown, rotted tip with shriveled kernels
- Some pink/reddish kernel discoloration
- Partial husk removal exposing the cob

This points to an ear rot disease. White mycelium starting from the base is characteristic of Diplodia Ear Rot. Let me verify with a reference image.

The reference Diplodia image shows bleached husks and mild kernel discoloration, but doesn't match the heavy white mycelium in the test image as closely.

Reconsidering the test image:
- White mycelium growing from the base area of the ear
- Brown/rotted tip with shriveled kernels
- Some pink/reddish kernel coloration in the middle section

The white mycelium starting at the base strongly matches Diplodia Ear Rot's description. The tip browning and kernel rot are consistent with advanced Diplodia infection. The pink tinge could be co-infection but the dominant pattern (white mycelium from base) is Diplodia.
